public_rationale: At the end of 2025 the US still had no comprehensive federal AI law (e2). In December 2025 federal policy moved to challenge state AI rules instead of adding consumer protections (e1). Some narrow protections did appear: the federal Take It Down Act on deepfake intimate images (e3), and California's companion-chatbot law SB 243 (e4). These are real but limited to one harm or one state. On a plain reading, the US still had very little regulation protecting consumers from generative-AI risks, so the forecast holds. Narrow laws keep it from being clear-cut.
limitations: 'Very little' has no threshold; a reader who weighs state laws and the Take It Down Act heavily could call this mixed.
The review did not catalogue every state law enacted in 2025.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: through the end of 2025, the US would have no broad, binding rules that protect consumers from generative-AI risks. Any protections would stay narrow, partial, or not yet in force.

Federal law and state law both count. A few narrow statutes do not by themselves make the forecast false. A comprehensive federal or widely applicable consumer-protection regime for generative AI in force during 2025 would.
criteria.support_condition: By end-2025 there is no comprehensive federal law on generative-AI consumer risks. Federal policy stays light-touch or deregulatory. State rules are narrow, piecemeal, or not yet in force.
criteria.contradiction_condition: During 2025 the US enacts and brings into force broad, binding consumer protections against generative-AI risks, such as a federal AI consumer-protection statute or widely applicable state regimes in effect.

evidence.explanation: A law-firm review written after 2025 confirms that no comprehensive federal AI law existed as of the end of 2025, and that federal policy was light-touch.

evidence.excerpt: In May 2025, President Trump signed the Take It Down Act, legislation championed by the First Lady to protect young Americans from deepfake exploitation online.
evidence.explanation: A federal law signed in 2025 does address one generative-AI harm, deepfake intimate images. That partly cuts against 'very little', though its scope is narrow.
